title: Whitehall 1212
paragraphs: A Scotland Yard crime drama built from cases in the Black Museum files, emphasizing the police investigation and evidence that lead from the discovery of a crime to its solution.

NBC police-procedural true-crime anthology based on Scotland Yard case files and Black Museum evidence. The GRH container holds one audition, 43 surviving regular broadcasts, and two OTRR reference tracks; regular episode #2 is missing from circulation.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: NBC regular run (November 18, 1951 to September 28, 1952) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Percy Hoskins (performer and researcher), Wyllis Cooper (director and writer), Harvey Hayes (performer), Lester Fletcher (performer), Horace Braham (performer), Lionel Ricou (announcer), and Guy Spaull (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

The stories often return to historical true crime case, police investigation and Scotland Yard procedure, Black Museum evidence object, forensic and physical evidence, murder and homicide, and burglary, theft and property crime.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Scotland Yard Black Museum as evidentiary frame, NBC true-crime drama with an all-British cast, Whitehall 1212 and The Black Museum overlap, and Police-procedural viewpoint in early-1950s radio.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|cloak-and-dagger|Cloak and Dagger]], [[show|quiet-please|Quiet Please]], [[show|the-chase|The Chase]], [[show|nbc-university-theater|NBC University Theater]], and [[show|stroke-of-fate|Stroke of Fate]].
